title: I fell on my hand
goal: Playing football with Sēf, you fall on your hand: say what hurts, then let him take you to A&E
tip: ṭāḥ 'he fell' gives ṭiḥt 'I fell', as rāḥ gives riḥt. A hand is feminine, so its verb and participle are feminine too: īdi tʿawwirni 'my hand hurts', maksūra 'broken'. A head is masculine: rāsi yʿawwirni.
grammar: recycle: hollow-verb past (ṭiḥt) and a feminine body part (īdi tʿawwirni, maksūra)
dialogue: A
شفيك؟ طحت؟
shfīk? ṭiḥt?
What's wrong? Did you fall?
B
هيه، طحت. إيدي تعورني وايد
hē, ṭiḥt. īdi tʿawwirni wāyid
Yes, I fell. My hand really hurts.
A
سلامات! تقدر تحركها؟
salāmāt! tigdar tḥarrik-ha?
Oh no! Can you move it?
B
الله يسلمك. شوي بس. يمكن مكسورة؟
allāh ysallmak. shwayy bas. yimkin maksūra?
Thanks. Only a little. Could it be broken?
A
إن شاء الله مب مكسورة، بس لازم نروح الطوارئ
in shāʼ allāh mub maksūra, bas lāzim nrūḥ iṭ-ṭawāriʼ
Hopefully it isn't broken, but we have to go to A&E.
B
مب لازم! بحط عليها ثلج وبرتاح
mub lāzim! baḥuṭṭ ʿalēha thalj w bartāḥ
There's no need! I'll put ice on it and rest.
A
لا والله. لازم يسوون لك أشعة، يمكن شي خطير
la wallāh. lāzim ysawwūn-lak ashiʿʿa, yimkin shay khaṭīr
No way. You need an X-ray. It could be something serious.
B
زين، يلا. بس سوق شوي شوي!
zēn, yalla. bas sūg shwayy shwayy!
OK, let's go. But drive slowly!
items: I fell; you fell (to a man)
to a woman: ṭiḥti (طحتي); he fell: ṭāḥ (طاح)
a hand, an eye or an ear takes tʿawwirni; a masculine part takes yʿawwirni: rāsi yʿawwirni
can you move it (f.)? (to a man)
to a woman: tigdarīn tḥarrkīnha? (تقدرين تحركينها؟); a masculine thing: tigdar tḥarrkah?
broken (a feminine thing, such as a hand)
a masculine thing: maksūr (مكسور); inkisar = it broke
lāzim ysawwūn-lak ashiʿʿa = you need an X-ray (lit. they have to do an X-ray for you) (to a man); to a woman: lāzim ysawwūn-lich ashiʿʿa
to a woman: sūgi shwayy shwayy (سوقي شوي شوي)
culture: Visiting the sick (ʿiyādat il-marīẓ) is a recommended act in Islam. When you hear that someone is ill or hurt, call or visit, and say salāmāt or ma tshūf shar. The answer is allāh ysallmak (to a woman: allāh ysallmich).

title: At the A&E desk
goal: At the A&E desk, tell the receptionist (a woman) what happened, show your insurance card and ask about the wait
tip: The future is b- + the present verb for every person: bitnādīk 'she'll call you', biyshūfak 'he'll see you', batrayya 'I'll wait'. For 'if it gets worse', use idha + past: idha ṣārat akhass, bagūl-lich 'if it gets worse, I'll tell you'.
grammar: recycle: future b- for I, he and she (batrayya, biyshūfak, bitnādīk); idha + past
dialogue: B
السلام عليكم. طحت على إيدي، وتعورني وايد
as-salāmu ʿalaykum. ṭiḥt ʿala īdi, w tʿawwirni wāyid
Hello. I fell on my hand, and it really hurts.
A
وعليكم السلام. سلامات! عندك تأمين؟
wa ʿalaykum is-salām. salāmāt! ʿindak taʼmīn?
Hello. Oh dear! Have you got insurance?
B
الله يسلمج. هيه، هذي بطاقة التأمين
allāh ysallmich. hē, hādhi biṭāgat it-taʼmīn
Thank you. Yes, this is the insurance card.
A
زين. تفضل اقعد هناك، والممرضة بتناديك
zēn. tfaẓẓal igʿid hnāk, w il-mumarriẓa bitnādīk
OK. Please take a seat over there, and the nurse will call you.
B
بتريا وايد؟
batrayya wāyid?
Will I be waiting long?
A
ما أدري. الحين الانتظار طويل، يمكن ساعة
ma adri. il-ḥīn il-intiẓār ṭawīl, yimkin sāʿa
I don't know. There's a long wait now, maybe an hour.
B
زين. بس إذا صارت أخس، بقول لج
zēn. bas idha ṣārat akhass, bagūl-lich
OK. But if it gets worse, I'll tell you.
A
أكيد. والدكتور بيشوفك أول ما يفضى
akīd. w id-daktōr biyshūfak awwal ma yifẓa
Of course. And the doctor will see you as soon as he's free.
items: have you got insurance? (to a man)
to a woman: ʿindich taʼmīn? (عندج تأمين؟)
a man: il-mumarriẓ (الممرض); you'll also hear is-sistar (السستر) for a woman nurse
she'll call you (by name) (to a man)
to a woman: bitnādīch (بتناديج); he'll call you: biynādīk (بيناديك)
the wait, waiting (at a clinic, an office)
il-intiẓār ṭawīl = there's a long wait
a masculine thing: ṣār akhass (صار أخس)
about a woman: awwal ma tifẓa (أول ما تفضى)

title: Did the insurance cover it?
goal: Back at the office, tell Maryam what the doctor said and what the insurance did and didn't cover
tip: ghaṭṭa 'it covered' is Form II, like sawwa: present yghaṭṭi. Pass on what the doctor said with gāl inn-: gāl innha mub maksūra 'he said it isn't broken'. Ask with idha 'whether': isʼalhum idha… 'ask them whether…'.
grammar: recycle: reported speech (gāl innha), idha 'whether' and Form II (ghaṭṭa)
dialogue: A
صباح الخير! شو صار في إيدك؟
ṣabāḥ il-khēr! shu ṣār fi īdak?
Good morning! What happened to your hand?
B
صباح النور. طحت وأنا ألعب كورة
ṣabāḥ in-nūr. ṭiḥt w ana alʿab kūra
Morning. I fell while I was playing football.
A
ما تشوف شر! مكسورة؟
ma tshūf shar! maksūra?
I hope it's nothing serious! Is it broken?
B
الله يسلمج. لا، الدكتور قال إنها مب مكسورة
allāh ysallmich. la, id-daktōr gāl innha mub maksūra
Thank you. No, the doctor said it isn't broken.
A
الحمد لله. والتأمين غطى العلاج؟
il-ḥamdu lillāh. w it-taʼmīn ghaṭṭa l-ʿilāj?
Thank God. And did the insurance cover the treatment?
B
غطى الأشعة، بس الدوا دفعته من جيبي
ghaṭṭa l-ashiʿʿa, bas id-dawa difaʿtah min jēbi
It covered the X-ray, but I paid for the medicine out of my own pocket.
A
غريبة! دق عليهم واسألهم إذا بيرجعون لك الفلوس
gharība! digg ʿalēhum w isʼalhum idha biyrajjʿūn-lak il-flūs
That's odd! Ring them and ask them whether they'll give you the money back.
B
زين، بدق على شركة التأمين وبسألهم إذا يغطون الدوا
zēn, badigg ʿala sharikat it-taʼmīn w basʼalhum idha yghaṭṭūn id-dawa
OK, I'll ring the insurance company and ask them whether they cover medicine.
items: what happened to your hand? (to a man)
to a woman: shu ṣār fi īdich? (شو صار في إيدج؟)
w ana + a present verb = while I was …-ing: ṭiḥt w ana amshi = I fell while I was walking
present: yghaṭṭi (يغطي); it covered it (f.): ghaṭṭāha (غطاها)
I paid for it (m.) out of my own pocket
a feminine thing: difaʿt-ha (دفعتها); I paid: difaʿt (دفعت)
ask them whether, ask them if (to a man)
to a woman: isʼalīhum idha (اسأليهم إذا)
they'll give you the money back (to a man)
to a woman: biyrajjʿūn-lich il-flūs (بيرجعون لج الفلوس)
culture: In Dubai, a 2013 law makes employers provide basic health insurance for their staff, and sponsors for the people they sponsor. What a plan covers differs from one policy to the next, so it's normal to ring the insurer or ask HR when a bill isn't covered.

title: My wallet's gone!
goal: After coffee with Sēf at a mall café you can't find your wallet: say what's in it, think back to where you last had it and decide what to do
tip: ẓāʿ 'it got lost' needs no doer, like ṭāḥ 'it fell': ẓāʿ būki 'my wallet's gone'. ẓayyaʿt 'I lost' says who did it. insarag 'it got stolen' is Form VII, like inkisar 'it broke'. Set the scene with kint gāʿid: kint gāʿid adfaʿ 'I was paying'.
grammar: recycle: ẓāʿ 'it got lost' vs ẓayyaʿt 'I lost'; Form VII (insarag); kint gāʿid for the background
dialogue: B
سيف! ضاع بوكي!
Sēf! ẓāʿ būki!
Sēf! My wallet's gone!
A
لا تحاتي. وين ضيعته؟ متى آخر مرة شفته؟
la tḥāti. wēn ẓayyaʿtah? mita ākhir marra shiftah?
Don't worry. Where did you lose it? When did you last see it?
B
في الكوفي. كنت قاعد أدفع الحساب
fi l-kōfi. kint gāʿid adfaʿ il-ḥsāb
At the café. I was paying the bill.
A
يمكن طاح منك هناك. ولّا يمكن انسرق؟
yimkin ṭāḥ minnak hnāk. walla yimkin insarag?
Maybe you dropped it there. Or maybe it got stolen?
B
ما أدري! كل بطاقاتي فيه، حتى بطاقة التأمين
ma adri! kill biṭāgāti fīh, ḥatta biṭāgat it-taʼmīn
I don't know! All my cards are in it, even the insurance card.
A
خلنا نرجع الكوفي. يمكن أحد لقاه
khallna nirjaʿ il-kōfi. yimkin aḥad ligāh
Let's go back to the café. Maybe someone found it.
B
وإذا ما لقيناه، شو أسوي؟
w idha ma ligēnāh, shu asawwi?
And if we don't find it, what do I do?
A
دق على البنك أول، وبعدين بنروح مركز الشرطة
digg ʿala l-bank awwal, w baʿdēn binrūḥ markaz ish-shurṭa
Ring the bank first, and then we'll go to the police station.
items: my wallet's gone, I've lost my wallet (lit. my wallet got lost)
your wallet (to a man): būkak (بوكك); you'll also hear maḥfaẓa (محفظة)
when did you last see it (m.)? (to a man)
to a woman: mita ākhir marra shiftīh? (متى آخر مرة شفتيه؟)
maybe you dropped it (lit. maybe it fell from you) (to a man)
to a woman: yimkin ṭāḥ minnich (يمكن طاح منج)
it got stolen, it was stolen
a feminine thing: insargat (انسرقت); UAE also: inbāg (انباق)
all my cards are in it (m.)
in a feminine thing, such as a bag: fīha (فيها)
a feminine thing: ligāha (لقاها); UAE also: ḥad (حد) for aḥad
to a woman: diggi ʿala l-bank (دقي على البنك)

title: At the police station
goal: At a Dubai police station, report your lost wallet to an officer: say when and where it went missing and describe it
tip: Describe a lost thing with kān: kān fīh 'there was … in it', kān fīh khams miyat dirham. Say what you don't know with an indirect question: ma adri wēn ṭāḥ 'I don't know where I dropped it'. ẓāyiʿ 'lost' is a participle, like rāyiḥ: a feminine thing is ẓāyʿa.
grammar: recycle: kān for a past description (kān fīh); indirect questions (ma adri wēn); participles (ẓāyiʿ)
dialogue: B
السلام عليكم. أبي أبلغ عن بوك ضايع
as-salāmu ʿalaykum. abi aballigh ʿan būk ẓāyiʿ
Hello. I'd like to report a lost wallet.
A
وعليكم السلام. زين، متى ضاع، ووين؟
wa ʿalaykum is-salām. zēn, mita ẓāʿ, w wēn?
Hello. OK, when was it lost, and where?
B
اليوم الظهر في كوفي في المول. بس ما أدري وين طاح
il-yōm iẓ-ẓuhur fi kōfi fi l-mōl. bas ma adri wēn ṭāḥ
Today at midday, at a café in the mall. But I don't know where I dropped it.
A
شو لونه؟ وشو كان فيه؟
shu lōnah? w shu kān fīh?
What colour is it? And what was in it?
B
لونه أسود. كان فيه بطاقاتي وخمس مية درهم
lōnah aswad. kān fīh biṭāgāti w khams miyat dirham
It's black. My cards and five hundred dirhams were in it.
A
زين، بكتب البلاغ. عطني رقمك
zēn, baktib il-balāgh. ʿaṭni ragmak
OK, I'll write up the report. Give me your number.
B
تفضل. تتوقع بتلقونه؟
tfaẓẓal. titwaggaʿ bitilgūnah?
Here you go. Do you think you'll find it?
A
إن شاء الله. وايد ناس يسلّمون الأغراض اللي يلقونها
in shāʼ allāh. wāyid nās ysallmūn il-aghrāẓ illi yilgūnha
Hopefully. A lot of people hand in the things they find.
items: I'd like to report (something to the police)
I told the police, I reported (it) to the police: ballaght ish-shurṭa (بلغت الشرطة)
when was it lost? when did it go missing?
a feminine thing: mita ẓāʿat? (متى ضاعت؟)
a feminine thing: shu lōnha? (شو لونها؟)
there was … in it (m.), it had … in it
in a feminine thing: kān fīha (كان فيها)
give me your number (to a man)
to a woman: ʿaṭīni ragmich (عطيني رقمج)
do you think so? do you expect…? (to a man)
they hand in, they hand over
he hands in: ysallim (يسلّم); don't mix it up with ysallim ʿala (يسلم على) = he says hi to
culture: Dubai Police say they returned more than 171,000 found items to their owners in 2025. Found things can be handed in at police stations and at some shopping centres, so it's worth reporting a loss even when you think it's gone for good.

title: Checkpoint 3.6: the wallet turns up
goal: Checkpoint: Fahad and Sēf wait outside while you collect your wallet from the police; tell Fahad (A) what happened and how your hand is, and thank them both
tip: A Kuwaiti says shṣār? for shu ṣār? 'what happened?'. A feminine thing takes feminine verbs: biṭāgat it-taʼmīn ẓāʿat 'the insurance card's gone', ṣārat aḥsan 'it's got better'. il-ghada ʿalay 'lunch is on me' becomes il-ghada ʿalēna 'lunch is on us'.
grammar: checkpoint 3.6: recycle s3u084–s3u100 (health, insurance, losing things)
dialogue: A
شصار؟ البوك وياك؟
shṣār? il-būk wiyyāk?
What happened? Have you got the wallet?
B
هيه! واحد لقاه في المول وسلّمه للشرطة
hē! wāḥid ligāh fi l-mōl w sallamah lish-shurṭa
Yes! Someone found it at the mall and handed it in to the police.
A
الحمد لله! وكل شي فيه؟
il-ḥamdu lillāh! w kill shay fīh?
Thank God! And is everything in it?
B
الفلوس والبطاقات كلها، بس بطاقة التأمين ضاعت
il-flūs w il-biṭāgāt killha, bas biṭāgat it-taʼmīn ẓāʿat
All the money and the cards, but the insurance card's gone.
A
عادي. وإيدك؟ رحت المستشفى مرة ثانية؟
ʿādi. w īdak? riḥt il-mustashfa marra thānya?
Never mind. And your hand? Did you go to the hospital again?
B
لا، ما يباله، صارت أحسن. يا شباب، ما قصرتوا وياي
la, ma yabā-lah, ṣārat aḥsan. yā shabāb, mā gaṣṣartu wiyyāy
No, there's no need, it's got better. Guys, you've been so good to me.
A
ما سوينا شي! يلا، الغدا علينا اليوم
mā sawwēna shay! yalla, il-ghada ʿalēna l-yōm
We didn't do anything! Come on, lunch is on us today.
B
لا والله، هالمرة علي!
la wallāh, hal-marra ʿalay!
No way, this time it's on me!
items: he handed it (m.) in to the police
it (f.) got lost, it's gone missing
it (f.) has got better, it's better now
a masculine thing: ṣār aḥsan (صار أحسن); worse: ṣārat akhass
